name: Bullish Double Vertical (Call Debit + Put Credit)
summary: Buy a call debit spread and finance it by selling a put credit spread in the same expiry - a defined-risk directional bullish structure that can often be opened for a small debit or even a credit.

legs.strike_rule: short put strike minus width Wp
long call strike plus width Wc, placed at the upside price target

max_profit: (Wc - net debit) x 100, or (Wc + net credit) x 100 if opened for a credit - achieved above the short call strike
max_loss: (Wp + net debit) x 100, or (Wp - net credit) x 100 - achieved below the long put strike
breakevens: if opened for a debit: long call strike + net debit per share, and short put strike - (Wp ... ) - compute the exact lower breakeven numerically at entry and store it

greeks.gamma: mixed, slightly negative near the short strikes
greeks.theta: slightly positive when the put credit spread dominates

when_to_use: Directionally bullish with IV rank >= 25 (so the put spread pays for the call spread) and a defined upside target. Preferable to a naked long call spread when IV is elevated and you are willing to accept downside risk to the put spread.
entry_rules: Bullish trigger required: price above the 50-day SMA AND 20-day SMA slope positive, or a defined breakout above the 20-day high
Net cost <= 25% of Wc (the call spread width), i.e. the put spread must finance at least 75% of the call spread
Short put at 0.20-0.25 delta; short call at the target price (measured move or 20-day ATR x 2 above spot)
DTE 30-60, no earnings inside the expiry
OI >= 500, spread <= 10% of mid on all four legs
management_rules: Take profit at 60% of max profit
Roll or close the put spread at 50% of ITS credit if the call spread is still open and working
Loss stop: close everything if the loss reaches 1.0x the maximum profit of the call spread (asymmetric structures need a tighter loss rule than symmetric ones)
Trend invalidation: close if price closes below the 50-day SMA
Never add to the losing put side
exit_rules: Force-close by 15:45 ET on expiration day, always
Close the put vertical immediately if the short put goes ITM by more than 0.25 x Wp, or its delta <= -0.85, or its extrinsic < $0.10
Close the call vertical immediately if the short call goes ITM and its extrinsic < $0.10 (it is at max profit there anyway)
Ex-dividend guard on the short call
assignment_risk: Both verticals contain a short leg. The short put is the live one in a decline (obligation to buy 100 shares per contract); the short call only goes ITM at maximum profit, where the structure should be closed anyway.
buying_power: Max of the two verticals' requirements, typically (Wp - put credit) x 100 per contract, plus any net debit on the call side.
common_mistakes: Treating the financed call spread as free - the put spread carries real downside risk; setting the short call below a realistic target and capping the trade too early; carrying the short put through a sharp decline.
zero_dte_notes: Usable intraday as a directional 0DTE structure on SPY/QQQ after a confirmed trend signal (price above VWAP with rising volume). Use 0.15 delta short put, target the short call at the measured move, take profit at 50% of max, hard stop at 1x the call spread's max profit, force-close 15:45 ET.
family: four-leg structures (iron condors, iron butterflies, condors, double calendars/diagonals, boxes, jelly rolls, conversions/reversals, double verticals, double ratio spreads)
